prompt: Users are annoyed that the assistant forgets their dietary restrictions every time they start a new chat.
tells: every time they start a new chat
why: Save durable facts to a memory store and load relevant ones into each new session.
trap: Within one chat the context holds it; across chats you need memory.

prompt: A coding agent works on a project over several days and must pick up where it left off, including decisions made earlier.
tells: pick up where it left off
why: Persist notes and decisions (for example a progress file) that later sessions read first.
trap: The loop runs within a session; continuity across sessions needs memory.

prompt: When a user corrects the agent ("our fiscal year starts in April"), it should apply that correction in all future conversations.
tells: apply that correction in all future conversations
why: Write the correction to long-term memory and recall it when relevant.
trap: Fine-tuning per user would be far too heavy for one fact.

prompt: A companion app has two years of conversations per user, far too much to include, but it should recall relevant past moments when they come up.
tells: two years of conversations per user
why: Store memories outside the context and retrieve the relevant ones per turn.
trap: Summarizing everything into one prompt loses the specifics people care about.

prompt: A support agent should know, when a customer returns next month, which fixes were already tried last time.
tells: when a customer returns next month
why: Persist a case history and load it when the customer comes back.
trap: A ticket-system tool could hold it too, but the need is recall across sessions.

prompt: A writing assistant should gradually learn that this user prefers short sentences and no exclamation marks, and keep applying that.
why: Save observed preferences to memory and include them in future prompts.
trap: A critic could enforce style within one draft, not remember it between sessions.

prompt: An assistant keeps telling a user about their old job, because it saved that fact months ago and never updated it.
why: Memory needs updating and expiry, not just writing: let the agent revise or forget outdated facts.
trap: It looks like a quality bug, but the cause is how memories are maintained.

prompt: An internal agent should remember decisions made in earlier planning sessions, such as which database the team chose and why.
tells: remember decisions made in earlier planning sessions
why: Write decisions to a durable store the agent consults in later sessions.
trap: Nothing here is split into subtasks; it's continuity over time.
